title: Goldman Raises S&P 500 Target, Sees 17% Upside This Year - Yahoo Finance
text: Goldman Raises S&P 500 Target, Sees 17% Upside This Year Khac Phu Nguyen May 28, 2026 1 min read GS ^GSPC MS This article first appeared on GuruFocus . Goldman Sachs ( NYSE:GS ) has joined Morgan Stanley ( NYSE:MS ) and Deutsche Bank in projecting further upside for the S&P 500 ( SPY ), raising its year-end target to 8,000 from 7,600 as AI-driven earnings momentum continues to power the market. Strategists led by Ben Snider now see a possible 17% return for the index this year, arguing that continued earnings growth could keep driving US equities higher after an exceptionally strong first-quarter reporting season. Warning! GuruFocus has detected 9 Warning Signs with GS. Is GS fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator. The S&P 500 has already climbed almost 10% this year, fueled by a tech rally as investors focus on strong earnings despite geopolitical and economic fallout from the Iran war. The benchmark closed at a fresh record of 7,519 on Tuesday, while Goldman also lifted its 2026 earnings-per-share forecast for S&P 500 companies to $340, implying 24% year-on-year growth. The firm expects EPS to rise another 13% in 2027. Goldman's key message is that AI remains central to the earnings story, but valuation upside may still face limits. The strategists said companies benefiting from AI infrastructure investment should contribute roughly half of S&P 500 EPS growth this year, while decelerating earnings growth, AI uncertainty, macroeconomic risks, and interest rates could possibly prevent a major expansion in valuations.
